extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers, editors, and storytellers seeking a diagnostic framework for story structure
extracted.subtask_description: A practical framework for diagnosing and constructing fiction using Shawn Coyne's Story Grid: ensure every unit of story contains five essential story events, track per-scene metrics, and satisfy genre and controlling-idea requirements. Useful for writers and editors auditing scenes, sequences, acts, and whole novels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inciting Incident
rubrics_metrics.description: An unexpected event that destabilizes the protagonist by upsetting the balance of their life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two types noted: Causal — the protagonist actively chose; Coincidental — it happened to them. Must function to destabilize the protagonist and set story motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turning Point (Progressive Complication)
rubrics_metrics.description: The protagonist's strategies fail; conditions worsen until a final turning point — a revelation or action that forces a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents the 'things get worse' pressure that escalates stakes and moves the protagonist toward the crisis. Should show progressive worsening rather than stagnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: A binary choice with meaningful stakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two forms: Best Bad Choice — two terrible options; Irreconcilable Goods — two desirable options that cannot coexist. The crisis must force a clear, high-stakes decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climax
rubrics_metrics.description: The active answer to the question raised by the crisis; the decision under pressure that reveals true character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Climax must be an active choice/act, not passive. It should directly answer the crisis and disclose the protagonist's true nature or shift in character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The meaningful consequences of the climactic choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must validate the climax without being repetitious — focus on aftereffects, not restatement. Show how the world/relationships/value at stake have changed as a result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five Commandments present at every story level (fractal application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every functional unit of story (beat, scene, sequence, act, global story) must contain all five commandments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the five commandments fractally: beat (smallest unit of change), scene (single location/time), sequence (collection of related scenes), act/quadrant, and the global story. A failure at any level (e.g., a scene missing a commandment) is a structural defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlling Idea
rubrics_metrics.description: Every effective story communicates a single controlling idea — typically: "[Value] arises in human life when [cause]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The controlling idea is the truth the story argues. It must be coherent and consistently supported by events and character choices; an incoherent controlling idea is a basis for declaring a story failed.

rubrics_metrics.name: External and Internal Genre success
rubrics_metrics.description: A story must succeed in both its external genre and its internal genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External genre examples: action, war, society, performance (plot/outer conflict). Internal genre examples: worldview, status, morality, education (psychological/value change). Evaluate story against both tracks; failing either is a failure of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre Five-Leaf Clover (genre identification components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Five mandatory components of any genre identification: Time, Reality, Style, Structure, Content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time — long form, short form, etc.; Reality — realism, fantasy, etc.; Style — drama, comedy, etc.; Structure — arch-plot, miniplot, antiplot; Content — the value at stake. All five must be specified to correctly identify and judge a genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Grid spreadsheet scene metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: For every scene, track a diagnostic table of key metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields to record per scene include: Word count; Story event; Value shift (positive to negative, or vice versa); Polarity shift; Turning point; Point of view; Period / duration / location; Onstage characters; The five commandments present in that scene. Use this table to spot missing commandments, flat value arcs, pacing issues, and POV/continuity problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value Shift requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A scene must contain a value shift (positive to negative or vice versa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no value shift occurs the scene is considered failing. Track polarity shifts and value trajectories to ensure momentum and change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluative failure conditions (scene and story level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria describing when a scene or story should be judged as failing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scene fails if it lacks any of the Five Commandments or if no value shift occurs. Story fails if external + internal genres are not both fulfilled, or if the controlling idea is incoherent. Use these as hard diagnostic rules when auditing a manuscript.
